title: Disney's 'Hexed' Casts Its Spell on Thanksgiving: A Teen Witch, a Three-Eyed Cat and a $200 Million Bet
excerpt: Disney's Hexed opened Wednesday in 3,725 theaters at 68% on Rotten Tomatoes, with $2.1M in previews and a five-day Thanksgiving opening projected at $35–50M.
content:
Walt Disney Animation Studios' newest original film, Hexed, opened in theaters Wednesday, November 25, arriving just in time for Thanksgiving — and carrying the weight of a studio trying to prove its original stories can still draw a holiday crowd.

The film is the studio's 65th animated feature, and it is an original, not a sequel or an adaptation. It runs 103 minutes and is rated PG. It opened in 3,725 theaters across North America.

A teen, her mother and a family secret

Hexed follows Billie Doe, an impulsive 16-year-old voiced by Hailee Steinfeld, who discovers she has magical powers after removing the charm bracelet her mother made her wear. The discovery hurtles her out of her suburban Ohio hometown of Plainsville and into Hexe, a vast realm of witches — and forces her to team up with her cautious mother, Alice, voiced by Rashida Jones, to uncover family secrets that could change the witch world forever.

The voice cast also includes two-time Academy Award winner Jodie Foster as Queen Celeste, the sinister ruler of Hexe — who turns out to be Alice's mother and Billie's grandmother — and Walton Goggins as Beef Roger Crummchuk, a reclusive three-eyed cat who forms an uneasy alliance with mother and daughter. Henry Winkler voices Nigel, a skittish potoo bird, and the cast also includes Tracey Ullman, Stephen Fry and Dan Stevens.

The film is directed by Fawn Veerasunthorn and Jason Hand, co-directed by Josie Trinidad, and produced by Roy Conli and Yvett Merino. The screenplay is by Walt Disney Animation Studios chief creative officer Jared Bush and Dana Ledoux Miller, with an original score by Kris Bowers. The world premiere was held at the El Capitan Theatre in Los Angeles.

Critics split: fresh, but barely

The first full reviews landed Tuesday, November 24, after Disney held them under embargo until noon ET. The early hours looked rough: the Rotten Tomatoes score sat at 57 percent before climbing through the day. As of Wednesday morning, Hexed held 68 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 57 reviews, with an average rating of 6.7 out of 10, and a 56 on Metacritic from 22 critics — a score the site calls mixed or average.

That makes it the second-best reviewed Walt Disney Animation Studios film in three years, behind only Zootopia 2 at 92 percent — but the praise has clustered around the visuals, the mother-daughter story and Goggins' scene-stealing cat, while the harsher reviews call the story familiar and the magic underpowered.

Families heading to the theater get a bonus: a new animated short, Lilo & Scratch, plays before the feature. Steinfeld has also released her version of The Cars' song "Magic" from the film.

The Thanksgiving box office test

The commercial stakes are high. The film carries a reported production budget of about $200 million, a figure reported by Deadline that Disney has not confirmed. It took in $2.1 million in previews and an estimated $7.8 million on its first day, according to Deadline's Wednesday estimates — a modest start for a film of that scale.

Forecasts for the five-day Thanksgiving weekend cluster between $35 million and $50 million, with BoxOffice Pro more optimistic at $50 million to $70 million. That would make it one of the biggest openings for an original animated film this decade — but well short of the franchise titles around it. The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, which opened last weekend to $120 million domestically and $225 million worldwide, is projected to lead the holiday frame, and Universal's Focker-In-Law opened the same day as Hexed.

Analysis: Disney's originals problem

The numbers matter because Disney's recent original animated films have struggled at this exact holiday. Strange World finished with $74 million worldwide in 2022, and Wish reached $255 million worldwide in 2023 — totals that still fell short of what a $200 million production needs. Hexed was built to break that pattern: a new world, a new heroine and a marketing push that put its $2.1 million preview gross ahead of Encanto's $1.5 million and Wish's $1.8 million.

The second weekend will be the real test. Holiday family audiences, not critics, decide whether an original animated film becomes a Thanksgiving tradition or a footnote — and with no new animated competition until Paramount's Angry Birds 3 in a month, Hexed has a clear runway if word of mouth holds. The opening numbers say families turned out for the previews. The rest of the holiday weekend will show whether they come back.
